A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GHAP research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison; visual inspection resolved extraction problems in tables and figure labels.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering-quality and efficiency experiments, pipeline ablations, and sensitivity studies in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains original rendering experiments and adds baseline comparisons, runtime and memory measurements, loss ablations, and MCMC and compaction-schedule experiments.

M1.justification: The core KD-tree partitioning, CTD-based reduction, weighted Gaussian updates and appearance-only fine-tuning remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 4.3 introduces experimentally tested LPIPS-augmented loss variants with L1:SSIM:LPIPS weights of 8:1:1 and 6:2:2. These are limited objective extensions; the default pipeline remains unchanged, and iterative compaction was already permitted in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same thirteen scenes from Tanks & Temples, Mip-NeRF 360 and Deep Blending. v2 adds the mic scene from NeRF-Synthetic for its KD-tree ablation, a limited extension to synthetic-scene coverage.

E2.justification: v1's direct compaction comparison evaluates LightGaussian and PUP-3DGS. v2 Tables 1 and 4 additionally evaluate Trimming the Fat, MesonGS, 3DGS-MCMC, LocoGS and Mini-Splatting with its own compaction. Mini-Splatting-D and AtomGS remain backbone experiments, so their earlier participation is not counted as new.

E3.justification: The existing 15K-training plus 15K-fine-tuning schedule is retained. Added experiments introduce native 30K end-to-end baseline runs, a 300K versus 3M-to-300K MCMC comparison, controlled loss-weight variants, and multiple compaction schedules ending at 10% retention. Efficiency evaluation also shifts from final rendering FPS to compaction runtime and memory. These are substantial additions to evaluation design, not evidence that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 retains the random-subsampling and appearance-refinement ablation, but adds LPIPS-loss experiments and repeated-compaction schedules. Its mic-scene depth study measures quality, runtime and memory, replacing v1's Truck depth-sensitivity curve. The earlier single-compaction timing sweep and standalone quality/FPS retention sweep are removed; v2 instead supplies comparative rate-distortion and compaction-cost curves.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals or statistical tests for the reported results. v2's checklist claims statistical-significance reporting, but the actual appendix results do not provide corresponding uncertainty estimates or procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive comparator, compaction-cost, loss, depth and scheduling results while retaining the main GHAP quality scores and Table 3 ablation values. Existing results also change: LightGaussian's 10% Tanks & Temples PSNR changes from 22.560 to 22.113, and the full Mini-Splatting-D primitive count changes from 1473K to 3132K on that dataset despite unchanged quality scores. Earlier FPS entries disappear. These are reporting changes, not demonstrated improvements under verified identical conditions.

T1.justification: The CTD definition, reduction objective and Appendix A convergence theorem remain unchanged. New Appendix B.2 derives KD-tree construction and blockwise computational costs, including O(rho*n*s) using n/s blocks. This limited theoretical addition conflicts with the retained Remark 1 expression O(rho*s^2*log n); it does not provide a new convergence proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about optimal-transport compaction, quality at 10% retention and compatibility with 3DGS pipelines are retained. v2's contribution list explicitly claims the first adaptation of GMR to 3DGS and elevates low-overhead, state-of-the-art computational efficiency to a central contribution. This modestly strengthens novelty and efficiency positioning.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning perceptual-versus-distortion trade-offs, excessive partitioning fragmenting primitives, and the limited benefit of repeated compaction, recommending longer appearance optimization. It also discusses higher compaction memory and LocoGS's larger primitive counts. The original input-quality limitation and geometric-regularization explanation for Kitchen improvements remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code link, a method-by-method experimental pipeline table, explicit exclusion of compression modules, and loss-weight and scheduling details. Conversely, v1's specified block size s=3000 and random per-block initialization are no longer disclosed. Hardware documentation becomes inconsistent: Appendix B.3 retains the 96-core/five-GPU description, while the checklist states 64 cores and one GPU. These substantially change reproducibility information without establishing an actual hardware switch.

R1.justification: The main related-work discussion is largely retained. v2 adds MesonGS and LocoGS references and an expanded MCMC comparison rationale, while removing references to Compressed 3D Gaussian Splatting, Scaffold-GS and ContextGS with the earlier compression-background discussion. Its explicit first-GMR-adaptation claim modestly sharpens research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the experimental narrative, places direct comparisons before plug-in results, integrates the earlier takeaways into discussion, and rewrites the conclusion. The appendices replace lengthy variant tutorials with complexity and experimental-protocol sections and reorganized analyses. A conference checklist and revised author affiliations are also added.

P2.justification: Comparison tables are redesigned with primitive-count columns, method groupings and highlighting, and new protocol and ablation tables appear. New multi-panel cost and loss plots replace earlier displays. The retained qualitative comparison moves from Figure 4 to Figure 5, gains highlighted regions and corrects swapped PSNR/SSIM labels. Figure 8's scene gallery is retained, while the document adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons, direct compaction-cost measurements and targeted loss/schedule studies make v2 more informative, while the code link and protocol table improve reproducibility support. The net gain is limited by removed FPS evidence and initialization details, plus reporting inconsistencies: Tables 2 and 4 give 596K versus 496K primitives for the same 20% Deep Blending setting, and the new complexity analysis conflicts with Remark 1. The added evidence improves coverage without fully resolving reliability concerns.
